doc.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023

title: Passing the high parts versus Kenton's no-pass rule
summary: Studio players passed high notes to the kid, but Kenton never allowed lead trumpet to pass or have off nights.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You know I was going to ask you about that passing the part because Bobby Shew had a similar story, that he was complaining about the high parts and Dalton Smith said, “Don’t you know about this thing called ‘pass it on?’”

Yeah. One of the things you have to learn, well you know the funny part is, with Stan Kenton you couldn’t pass. He would not allow the lead — you played lead trumpet you played every single chart. He would not allow passing.
Even if you were having an off night?
Didn’t matter. You’re not supposed to have off nights.
In the fine print in your contract.

Off nights. When you’re playing that hard like in the Kenton band, to sit on top of that big a band, number one it was a thrill to do that, in really a good high spot. But it’s — what was I going to say? I kind of lost my train of thought there.
